args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18 across us-east, us-west, and eu-west). Per the runbook, I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all production regions. v2.3.0 is now running in us-east, us-west, and eu-west. Service status after rollback: healthy=true, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production and should not be redeployed until it is fixed. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure and confirm the on-call engineer is satisfied with the v2.3.0 state.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **Why v2.3.0:** It is the most recent production release marked healthy. v2.3.1 is the unhealthy release that was running. Because v2.3.0 has previously been healthy in production, the rollback did not need change-manager approval.
- **Result:** After the rollback, checkout-api reports healthy with an error rate of 0.002, down from 0.18 on v2.3.1.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback, and the current state. It also notes that v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until it is fixed, and that v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging.

content.text: The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0. v2.3.1 is the unhealthy one currently running in all three regions. v2.3.0 has been healthy in production, so the rollback doesn't need change-manager approval. Rolling back now.
